claim.statement: IranTalent-linked reporting in February-April 2026 shows a severe demand-side hiring freeze after the internet cutoff: TejaratNews/Zoomit quoted IranTalent CEO Asiyeh Hatami saying hiring demand fell 57% after internet disruptions, compared with 35% during the 12-day war, and that SMEs saw a 74% demand drop in the first three weeks of the international-internet cutoff; Zoomit later reported IranTalent data showing a 78% year-over-year drop in spring job opportunities for specialists and educated workers, from an earlier comparable average of about 65k opportunities per month to roughly four of five opportunities absent.
claim.subject: IranTalent labor-market data
claim.object: large hiring-demand and job-opportunity collapse after internet disruptions

evidence.summary: TejaratNews/Zoomit quotes IranTalent CEO Asiyeh Hatami on 57% overall hiring-demand decline, 74% SME decline, 35% war-period comparison, hiring freezes at large companies, and internet businesses hit hardest.
Zoomit reports IranTalent data that spring specialist/educated-worker opportunities fell 78% year-over-year, from a comparable prior-year average near 65k opportunities/month.
The notes distinguish hiring demand and job-opportunity metrics from direct unemployment counts.

information_depth.rationale: The figures are attributed to a named employment platform and named CEO, and a later Zoomit report gives a second IranTalent metric. The underlying raw platform dataset was not retrieved.

assessment.uncertainty: These are hiring-demand and job-opportunity measures, not direct layoff or unemployment-insurance counts. Some causality is shared with war and broader economic activity, although the sources isolate the internet cutoff as a major driver.

claim.statement: JobVision data reported by Digiato shows the internet cutoff produced an asymmetric labor-market shock: during the 21-plus-day Jan/Feb cutoff, new job ads fell 64% while applications fell 34%; after partial restoration, applications were only about 8% below pre-crisis levels but new ads remained 30% lower. Internet-dependent roles were hit hardest, with digital marketing/SEO ads down 80% during the Google cutoff and still 70% lower afterward, content/graphic roles down 70% and still 50% lower, customer-support roles down 70% and still 40% lower, and technology roles down 60% and still 30% lower.
claim.subject: JobVision labor-market data
claim.object: job ads withdrew more sharply and recovered more slowly than job applications under the internet cutoff

evidence.summary: Digiato reports JobVision's job-ad, application, recovery, and role-category metrics for the Jan/Feb internet cutoff and compares them to the 12-day war shock.

information_depth.rationale: The source provides a named platform dataset, multiple quantitative cuts, and a clear distinction between employer-side ads and worker-side applications.

assessment.uncertainty: The dataset is from a private hiring platform and may not cover offline work or all digital-sector hiring channels.

claim.statement: Digiato reported JobVision data that more than 318k resumes were sent on 5 Ordibehesht 1405, a one-day record 50% above the previous record, while job ads were down compared with the same period the previous year. The article interprets this as a sign of broad layoffs or job insecurity and of unusually high job-seeker pressure against reduced opportunity supply.
claim.subject: JobVision job-seeker activity
claim.object: 318k-plus resumes in one day while job ads were down year-over-year

evidence.summary: Digiato reports the 318k-plus one-day resume record, 50% above the prior record, and lower job ads compared with the same period last year.

information_depth.rationale: The resume count is a direct platform metric, but interpreting the cause as layoffs or insecurity is a media/platform inference.

assessment.uncertainty: Resume volume can rise for several reasons; it indicates job-seeker pressure, not a direct count of newly unemployed workers.

claim.statement: On 26 April 2026, Iran International quoted Jahangir Aghazadeh, head of the internet commission at Tehran's Computer Trade Organization, saying Iran's internet cutoff causes up to 5k billion tomans/day in damage and that about one-fifth of workers at digital companies are at risk of layoff. This is a sector risk estimate, not an audited employment count.
claim.subject: Iran digital-company workers
claim.object: layoff risk for about one-fifth of the workforce under the internet cutoff

evidence.summary: Iran International reports Aghazadeh's daily damage estimate and one-fifth layoff-risk estimate, with NetBlocks' 58-day blackout marker.

information_depth.rationale: The source names a sector official and a clear proportion, but gives no survey frame or company list.

assessment.uncertainty: Use as a risk estimate and sector-official warning. It does not show how many layoffs have already occurred.

claim.statement: The state's documented response to digital-economy employment damage is targeted credit and selective access rather than broad restoration: Digiato reported a Ministry of Communications / Innovation Fund / Post Bank agreement for up to 2k billion tomans in loans to damaged digital-economy businesses at 15.33% interest, with three months grace and nine months repayment, explicitly aimed at preserving employment; Masalat/ISNA/EghtesadOnline reported at least 50% income losses for some online businesses, weekly ICT-ministry damage assessment, work with the Statistical Center, and Nasr-led freelancer organization so international-internet access can be restored to selected workers.
claim.subject: Iranian state response to digital-economy damage
claim.object: credit support and selective access rather than general internet restoration

evidence.summary: Digiato reports the 2k-billion-toman loan facility, interest, grace, repayment, eligibility assessment, and employment-preservation purpose.
Masalat/ISNA reports 50% income-loss estimates, weekly damage assessment, planned Statistical Center cooperation, and Nasr-led freelancer organization for international-internet access.

information_depth.rationale: The support-package details are concrete and the selective-access mechanism is described by officials and sector bodies.

assessment.uncertainty: The sources do not show disbursement totals, uptake, or whether the loans prevented layoffs.

claim.statement: Payamema/CITNA reported that a 25 April 2026 Sanandaj Chamber knowledge-based-businesses commission meeting described heavy internet-cutoff losses, some internet-dependent firms nearing bankruptcy, and some specialist workers becoming jobless. The same meeting discussed alleged operator overbilling during the international-internet cutoff.
claim.subject: Sanandaj internet-dependent knowledge-based businesses
claim.object: near-bankruptcy and some specialist joblessness under the blackout

evidence.summary: The article summarizes a local chamber meeting where the commission head said some firms neared bankruptcy and some specialist workers became jobless.

information_depth.rationale: The source gives local official meeting evidence but no company names or counts.

assessment.uncertainty: Treat as local corroboration of the mechanism, not a scalable national estimate.

question.text: Can actual unemployment-insurance records, firm layoff notices, or sector survey instruments quantify how many digital-economy workers lost jobs, as distinct from how many hiring opportunities disappeared?
question.why_it_matters: v43 verifies a severe hiring freeze through IranTalent and JobVision, but hiring-demand collapse is not the same metric as realized unemployment or layoffs.
question.resolution_criteria: Find official unemployment-insurance registration counts, labor-ministry filings, named company notices, Nasr/association survey methodology, or platform microdata that separates layoffs from hiring freezes and income/hour losses.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v43 - Hiring data confirms the digital labor freeze
synthesis.summary: The forty-third pass upgrades v42's weaker hiring-demand lead with source-near labor-platform metrics. IranTalent-linked reporting says hiring demand fell 57% after internet disruptions, SMEs fell 74% in the first three weeks of the international-internet cutoff, and spring specialist opportunities were down 78% year-over-year from a prior comparable average near 65k opportunities/month. JobVision data independently shows the employer side withdrawing more than the worker side: during the 21-plus-day Jan/Feb cutoff, new ads fell 64% while applications fell 34%; after partial restoration, applications were only about 8% below baseline but ads remained 30% lower, with internet-dependent roles still deeply depressed. A later JobVision report says more than 318k resumes were submitted in one day, 50% above the previous record, while ads were down year-over-year. Nasr-linked reporting adds a one-fifth layoff-risk estimate for digital-company workers, and local Sanandaj reporting gives ground-level corroboration that some specialist workers have become jobless. The state response remains credit and selective access: a 2k-billion-toman loan package and freelancer/approved-business connectivity efforts, not public restoration. Net: v43 still lacks a national unemployment count, but it converts the labor shock from anecdote into a platform-measured hiring freeze.
synthesis.limitations: The central remaining gap is realized unemployment. IranTalent and JobVision measure hiring opportunities, ads, resumes, and applications, not unemployment-insurance registrations. The one-fifth layoff-risk figure and Sanandaj jobless reports corroborate employment damage but are not audited denominators. Causality also overlaps with war, recession, inflation, and broader uncertainty, although the role-category breakdown points strongly to the internet cutoff as the distinctive channel.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis now rests on named hiring-platform metrics, sector-official layoff-risk estimates, local business reporting, and concrete state-response details while preserving the distinction between hiring freezes and realized unemployment.

operations.rationale: IranTalent-linked metrics directly answer the hiring-data part of the v42 follow-up while leaving unemployment-insurance and firm-notice denominators unresolved.
JobVision gives source-near job-ad and application metrics showing employer withdrawal persisted after partial restoration.
The one-fifth risk estimate is a useful sector-official pointer, but it needs survey or administrative backing before it can close the denominator question.
Credit support and selective freelancer/business access extend the earlier finding that Internet Pro-style access is managed exception rather than public restoration.

operations.reason: v43 preserves v42's labor-shock framing and adds source-near IranTalent and JobVision metrics showing a measured hiring freeze.
